newsitem.title: USA: Southern group to buy Berlin utility.
newsitem.headline: Southern group to buy Berlin utility.

text.p: Southern Co said Tuesday it has agreed to buy 25 percent of Berlin's electric utility, Berliner Kraft und Licht AG, for about $830 million.

Southern said it formed a consortium with two leading German utilities, PreussenElektra and Bayernwer, which will control 75 percent of the Berlin utility, known commonly as Bewag. The deal is subject to approval by Berlin's parliament and European regulators.
The Bewag stake became available after the city of Berlin decided to sell its 50.8 percent share of the company, Southern noted.
That 50.8 percent, combined with shares of Bewag controlled by PreussenElektra and Bayernwerk, makes it possible for the three to each hold 25 percent of Bewag.
PreussenElektra is owned by Veba AG, and Bayernwerk is owned by Viag AG.
"This is by far the most significant investment undertaken by an American company in continental Europe's electric utility industry," Southern Chairman A.W. Dahlberg said.
"This acquisition from the start will enhance earnings for Southern Company shareholders," he said.

"Bewag is a vertically integrated electric utility with a premier distribution system and access to high-voltage transmission lines connecting to other parts of Europe. It offers us an opportunity to capture growth in the world's second-largest integrated utility market.

"We see the same prospects for profitable ventures in continental Europe that we find now in the United States: energy marketing and trading, low-cost generation, efficient distribution and enhanced energy services to customers."
